key_insight: Cardiologent turns arrhythmia assessment from simple rhythm labeling into patient-level decision support by combining signal-level analysis, guideline retrieval, and expert-style critique.
clinical_relevance: It may help clinicians prioritize urgency and management by producing auditable, guideline-grounded conclusions for continuous cardiac monitoring rather than just detecting an arrhythmia.
method: Uses a multi-agent pipeline for ECG and wearable PPG windows to extract measured features and grounded readings.
Assembles window-level readings into a patient rhythm profile and reasons over the patient’s data with retrieved clinical guidelines.
Adds a critic agent to check each conclusion against the cited guideline before finalizing decisions.
evidence_signal: In evaluation across integrated diagnosis, clinical significance, and urgency/management, Cardiologent ranked highest on every patient-level task, and an LLM judge showed agreement with cardiologists similar to inter-cardiologist agreement (ICC 0.74, 0.66 vs 0.67).
watch_item: Performance is promising, but real-world use will still depend on robust validation across diverse populations, device signals, and clinical workflows.
paper_title: Cardiologent: Multi-Agent Clinical Decision Support for Patient-Level Arrhythmia Assessment, Urgency, and Management
